{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYsbt5A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCRTEU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 17, "title": "Enable sound by default on game start and add a volume slider", "body": "## Problem

The web player has functional four-channel audio, but the browser audio output is currently **opt-in for every session**. `web/src/audio.ts` initializes `Sound.enabled = false`, and `web/index.html` presents a separate **Enable sound** button. A player can load a cartridge, see the game running, and hear nothing until they notice and click that additional button. There is also no UI for adjusting playback volume.

We want normal game audio to be **on by default when a player starts a game**, without an extra sound-enabling click, plus a compact, accessible **0–100% volume slider** and mute/unmute control. This must respect browser autoplay restrictions; enabling audible playback before any user gesture cannot be guaranteed or required.

## Expected outcome

- A new visitor sees a compact sound control with audio **preferred on by default** at a reasonable, nonzero volume (suggested default: **70%**). When they click **Play demo** or otherwise use an explicit supported game-start gesture, the Web Audio context is created/resumed from the browser's user-activation event and audio works without separately clicking **Enable sound**. The shipped original demo is intentionally silent, so verify audible output using an original licensed sound-producing test ROM.
- Player controls contain an accessible **volume slider** (0–100%) with an adjacent meaningful **Mute / Unmute** control. Changing the slider immediately adjusts audible output during gameplay without restarting the emulated machine.
- The interface distinguishes the sound preference (on vs muted) from the actual Web Audio state (unlocked/running vs blocked/suspended/unavailable). It must not falsely display `Sound playing` when the browser has not allowed the context to start.
- The user can still play normally if their browser denies or does not support audio; offer concise recoverable guidance to click/tap to enable sound.

## Context and implementation guidance

Current code (inspect `main` again before editing):

- [`web/src/audio.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/audio.ts): owns a single `AudioContext`, high-pass filter and bounded playback queue. Current graph: sources → high-pass filter → destination. `enable()` requires explicit invocation and `enabled` is initially false. `pause()/resume()/disable()` manage scheduled sources and context state.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): wires `#sound` as a manual toggle; the `Play demo` flow asynchronously fetches a ROM, while local ROM loading uses a file picker and async array-buffer reads/hash. `setRunning()` calls sound pause/resume, and the emulation loop pushes samples. **Do not wait for the ROM fetch/file read before attempting to unlock audio**; transient user activation may have expired.
- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): compact dark player with `#sound` and playback controls. Preserve the game-first styling and mobile layout.
- [`web/scripts/compat.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/compat.mjs) and [`web/scripts/smoke.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/smoke.mjs) already test actual Web Audio buffers, playback and failure paths. Extend relevant checks instead of introducing a separate test framework.
- [MDN Web Audio autoplay guidance](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API/Best_practices) and [autoplay policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Autoplay): audible autoplay may be blocked until user activation; `AudioContext` creation/resume should be initiated from a genuine user event. No browser policy bypass or automatic sound on page load is required.
- Follow the repo [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), including English language and actual validation reporting.

### Functional requirements

1. **Default-on audio preference, browser-safe unlock**
   - The default sound *preference* for a new visitor is ON at the documented nonzero volume. Never unexpectedly start audible sound on initial page load without a user gesture.
   - Wire a direct attempt to create/resume `AudioContext` to the **same click/tap activation that initiates playback** (e.g. the synchronous part of `Play demo`, and the existing **Load ROM** button before opening the file chooser). Also allow an explicit sound-control click to retry unlocking if necessary. A previously unlocked context must be reused.
   - Do not treat asynchronous ROM fetches, `File.arrayBuffer()`, SHA-256 calculations or automatic `requestAnimationFrame` as guaranteed user activation. If an unlock attempt is blocked or remains suspended, show accurate state and a small direct user action to retry; gameplay continues silently until allowed.
   - Respect user-selected mute: a muted player should not be force-unmuted by Play, Restart, model switching, Resume, or a new ROM.

2. **Volume and mute UX**
   - Add a labeled `<input type="range">` or equivalently accessible native control (min 0, max 100, small step) and compact numeric/percent indication, near the existing sound control without crowding the toolbar or mobile viewport.
   - Use an output **`GainNode`** in the Web Audio chain (sources → high-pass filter → gain → destination, or an equivalent single gain stage). Slider changes update gain for current and future sound immediately; do not modify game-generated sample buffers, CPU, or audio emulation.
   - Mute/unmute must be unambiguous and accessible. Muting silences audible output immediately while preserving the previous nonzero slider level for restoration. A slider value of 0 should be silent, and raising the volume should recover audible playback in a predictable way without duplicate audio contexts.
   - Avoid clipping and disruptive jumps: clamp values to a safe range, and use a small scheduled gain ramp if practical. Keep 100% at unity gain (no additional amplification above the existing PCM output). Handle initially silent homebrew demo accurately.

3. **Preference persistence and lifecycle**
   - Persist the chosen mute state and volume locally (using existing browser-local storage conventions, separate from ROM saves) so returning visitors retain their preferences; first visit defaults ON and 70%. Invalid values or unavailable storage must fall back safely without breaking the player.
   - On pause, tab hide, pagehide, reset and ROM/model change, maintain the existing bounded buffer behavior and stop/suspend scheduled audio as appropriate; resume only when playing and allowed by browser policy. **No stale buffered audio or duplicated sources** on restart.
   - If Web Audio creation/resume fails, preserve gameplay and show a recoverable, truthful notice. Do not claim the user has audible output when the context is suspended. Audio failures should not block ROM loading or be misreported as emulation-core errors.

4. **Scope**
   - This is a **frontend output/control change**. Preserve the from-scratch Rust sound core, ROM loading, original demo, emulator controls, local-save behavior, and GitHub Pages build path. No additional sound emulation, new UI framework, third-party media, or server storage.
   - Keep the UI minimal: do not add a full audio settings page. Update the short Settings/Help guidance and README to reflect default-on *after interaction*, mute/volume, autoplay limitations, and the demo's deliberate silence.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fresh browser profile, sound preference is ON with a nonzero default (70%) and the displayed control is truthful: the browser is not falsely marked as actively playing audio before unlock.
- [ ] Clicking **Play demo** invokes audio activation from the click/tap event *before any awaited ROM fetch*. Choosing **Load ROM** similarly attempts activation while the initiating gesture is active, not only after file read/hash. Once allowed, loading a known original **audible** fixture through the file picker produces non-silent output without a separate `Enable sound` click.
- [ ] A 0–100% volume slider changes the effective `GainNode` level immediately during active output; tests cover 0%, an intermediate level, and 100%. Volume changes do not affect framebuffer, emulation progress or CPU/audio sample generation.
- [ ] Mute and unmute work before and after the context is unlocked, preserve the previous slider value, and do not auto-unmute on starting/pausing/restarting/changing model/loading ROM; repeated toggling does not create duplicate AudioContexts or grow scheduled buffers without bound.
- [ ] Volume and mute preferences survive reload/reopen; malformed or denied localStorage access is handled safely without breaking game startup. ROM identity/save persistence remains independent of audio settings.
- [ ] Autoplay-restricted, suspended, AudioContext-unavailable and resume-error paths are accurately represented and recoverable by explicit interaction; the emulator stays playable silently and never reports a successful sound unlock that did not occur.
- [ ] Native keyboard/desktop and mobile/touch controls remain accessible. Volume slider has a programmatic label, is keyboard adjustable, and the player toolbar has no horizontal overflow at 375px width.
- [ ] Extend and pass relevant Playwright browser tests (`npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat`) using only original CC0 sound fixtures; verify actual output gain, mute behavior, user-gesture activation, persistence, pause/visibility/restart cleanup and failure recovery. Browser-specific autoplay behavior may require an injected policy simulation; report what was simulated vs truly observed.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `npm run build:wasm`, and `npm run build` pass, and changed-file checks are reported accurately. Preserve existing GitHub Pages deployment setup and keep unnecessary dependencies/frameworks out of scope.
- [ ] README and Settings/Help describe browser autoplay restrictions accurately without promising sound before any user gesture; do not imply the original silent demo will play audio.

## Optional validation

Test the player on a physical mobile device and additional browser engines (Safari/Firefox) to observe actual autoplay and volume handling; these are optional, not pre-merge blockers.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** Confirm the existing `main` Pages workflow succeeds for the merged commit and record its Actions run URL.
2. **Pending:** Open the public player, start an original audio-generating licensed fixture with a normal user gesture, and verify default-on audio, the mute button and live volume adjustments. Reload to check remembered preferences, noting any actual browser autoplay restrictions.

These live-publication checks are after merge; they must not be asserted complete before deployment.
